## Objective

Retire the remaining legacy `adl/src` implementation after the ADL v1 rollback window closes, while preserving every still-supported behavior through ADL v2, Runtime v3, C-SDLC v2, or an explicitly owned adapter.

## Scheduling gate

- Do not begin destructive deletion before the retained ADL v1 rollback window ends on **2026-08-12T09:04:24Z**.
- Before deletion, verify whether rollback was invoked and confirm the selected ADL v2 generation remains healthy.
- This issue is scheduled for the **v0.92 backlog** and does not authorize changes during the rollback window.

## Dependencies

- WP-20

## Current baseline

- Original `adl/src` baseline: **355,675 physical Rust LoC across 621 files**.
- Current merged-tree `adl/src`: approximately **261,273 physical Rust LoC across 480 files**.
- Reduction so far: approximately **94,402 LoC (26.5%)**.
- Final target: at least **80% deletion** from the pinned baseline; **90% preferred**.
- `adl/src/runtime_v2` remains approximately **80,282 LoC** and is a primary post-cutover retirement candidate.

Refresh these measurements at execution start and pin the exact revision.

## Required work

1. Produce an exhaustive machine-readable inventory of every remaining `adl/src` module, binary, test surface, and active CI/install/documentation reference.
2. Classify each row as migrated to ADL v2, Runtime v3, C-SDLC v2, a named adapter/product owner, temporarily retained with owner/reason/expiry, or eligible for deletion.
3. Close all real capability gaps before deleting their incumbent implementation.
4. Make the thin ADL v2 CLI the supported `adl` entrypoint while preserving required command and artifact contracts.
5. Remove Runtime v2 and obsolete compatibility binaries after exact parity, rollback, and operational installation proof.
6. Remove stale `adl/Cargo.toml`, CI, coverage, installer, documentation, and demo references as their owning surfaces disappear.
7. Delete by bounded ownership band with focused validation and review; do not perform one opaque bulk deletion.
8. Publish exact before/after physical LoC, file counts, retained exceptions, and replacement owners.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rollback window completion and selector health are verified at an exact revision.
- [ ] Every remaining legacy file has a disposition and an accountable replacement owner.
- [ ] No supported behavior is represented only by deleted legacy code.
- [ ] The supported `adl` command resolves to the thin ADL v2 implementation.
- [ ] Runtime v2 is absent from production source and active build/CI routes.
- [ ] Active CI, installation, documentation, and examples no longer require the legacy crate.
- [ ] At least 80% of the pinned 355,675-line incumbent baseline is deleted, with 90% preferred.
- [ ] Any retained 80-89% exception has owner, reason, and expiry; below 80% is not completion.
- [ ] Focused parity, rollback, integration, and clean-install proofs pass on the exact deletion head.
- [ ] Final bounded review has no unresolved actionable findings.

## Non-goals

- Deleting code before a replacement capability is operational.
- Treating crate movement alone as simplification.
- Retaining unowned compatibility code indefinitely.

issues.body:
## Summary
The v0.91.8 review/repair flow exposed that CI and coverage are too broad, too slow, and too tightly coupled to lifecycle exact-SHA mechanics. Review-only or lifecycle-only deltas can trigger expensive broad Rust/coverage lanes, and exact-head/SHA churn repeatedly restarts checks. Create a v0.92 fix to simplify the CI/coverage process and reduce brittle SHA friction while preserving truthful review and merge safety.

## Problem
- Review/lifecycle-only updates can force full CI/coverage instead of focused documentation/control-plane checks.
- Coverage lanes still take too long and are difficult to reason about.
- Exact SHA / digest lifecycle mechanics are useful for truth but currently create excessive republish/recheck churn.
- Stale runs can keep burning CI minutes unless actively cancelled.
- The lane selector and lifecycle publication path need a cleaner separation between source/product changes, tooling changes, docs/review packets, and lifecycle metadata.

## Dependencies

- WP-02

## Scope
- v0.92 only; do not expand v0.91.8 scope.
- Use Gemini 3.1 Pro to review the current CI/coverage/lifecycle-publication process and suggest simplifications.
- Audit current GitHub Actions, validation lane selector, coverage lane sharding, and typed review/publish/finish exact-head contracts.
- Propose and implement a smaller, deterministic lane model that avoids duplicate or unnecessary heavy checks.
- Preserve exact-head safety for source/product merges, but remove avoidable SHA/digest churn for metadata-only lifecycle reconciliation where possible.
- Add automatic stale-run cancellation or repo-native guidance where safe.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Gemini review packet is retained locally/issue-bound and summarized into findings.
- Lane selector separates docs/review/lifecycle metadata from source/tooling/runtime changes with explicit PVF truth.
- Coverage lanes are parallelized and de-duplicated so we do not run the same coverage proof twice for the same PR class.
- Metadata-only typed lifecycle reconciliation no longer forces needless full heavy CI when the source merge candidate is already exact-head validated, or the remaining reason is documented and bounded.
- Exact-SHA/digest rules are simplified or wrapped so operators do not have to manually chase stale digests for ordinary publish/closeout.
- Tests cover lane selection and stale-run cancellation behavior.
- No AWS.

## Non-Goals
- No v0.91.8 release-tail scope expansion.
- No weakening source/product exact-head validation.
- No broad CI rewrite without retained compatibility and proof.

Closes: TBD when implemented.

## Summary

Restore `-D warnings` Clippy cleanliness for the CSM freedom-gate projection without changing runtime behavior.

## Problem

A focused production-binary Clippy run currently fails in `adl/src/csm_freedom_gate.rs` because two default-value expressions use unnecessary lazy closures:

- line 150: `executor_requires_gate_decision` uses `unwrap_or_else(|| json!(true))`
- line 151: `unmediated_execution_allowed` uses `unwrap_or_else(|| json!(false))`

Clippy reports `clippy::unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` and recommends eager `unwrap_or(...)` values. This is unrelated to Google Drive issue #5802 and must remain separately scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both warnings are removed with the smallest behavior-preserving Rust change.
- Existing freedom-gate defaults remain exactly `true` and `false`, respectively.
- Focused CSM freedom-gate tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --offline --bin adl-gws-context-mirror -- -D warnings` no longer fails on `csm_freedom_gate.rs`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes for the touched source.
- No unrelated runtime, Google Drive, lockfile, or dependency changes are included.

## Validation

- Focused tests covering `csm_freedom_gate`.
- Focused Clippy reproduction with `-D warnings`.
- `git diff --check`.

## Non-goals

- No freedom-gate semantic redesign.
- No broad Clippy cleanup outside the two observed warnings.
- No changes to issue #5802.

## Source Evidence

Observed during issue #5802 validation on 2026-08-04 with current Rust/Clippy: `clippy::unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` at `adl/src/csm_freedom_gate.rs:150-151`.

## Summary
Execute the bounded post-GitHub-migration build acceleration experiment defined in `.adl/docs/TBD/POST_GITHUB_MIGRATION_BUILD_ACCELERATION_EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md`. Compare the existing `ubuntu-latest` control with one restricted GitHub-hosted 16-core Ubuntu runner, preserve validation semantics, and make a retained adopt/reject/defer decision per measured lane.

## Required Outcome
A controlled, reversible experiment that determines whether selected ADL CI lanes become materially faster and cost-effective on a restricted 16-core GitHub-hosted runner without weakening exact-head proof, required checks, permissions, or fallback behavior.

## Dependencies
- WP-02 repository migration is verified through its post-transfer gate.
- WP-02A CI and coverage reliability establishes the trustworthy control topology.
- The destination organization has an eligible GitHub plan, owner-approved budget and alerts, and selected-repository runner-group approval.
- The experiment SHA, workflows, Rust toolchain, lockfiles, permissions, caches, artifacts, required checks, and branch protections are inventoried and frozen.

## Scope
- Retain a migration-eligibility receipt and frozen workload/environment manifest.
- Establish fresh same-SHA `ubuntu-latest` cold and warm controls for the shared smoke benchmark and representative Rust lanes.
- Configure one selected-repository 16-core Ubuntu larger-runner group with maximum concurrency one, bounded budget controls, least privilege, and a proven routing rollback.
- Run five cold and ten warm trials per candidate and workload, retaining queue, setup, cache, compile/link, execution, artifact, total-time, critical-path, reliability, and cost measurements.
- Prove output, artifact, and check-semantic parity before routing one canary lane.
- Produce a lane-by-lane adopt/reject/defer decision using the predeclared thresholds.
- If a lane is adopted, preserve required-check identity and standard-runner fallback and observe at least ten representative CI runs. If rejected, remove the experimental routing and configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Entry gates are verified from current migration, GitHub, billing, access, and CI evidence before any paid experiment runs.
- Control and candidate trials use the same exact commit, workflow, toolchain, lockfiles, commands, permissions, cache design, and proof inputs.
- Every warm run has cache-hit evidence; cold and warm samples, outliers, queue delay, failures, retries, and cancellations are retained without selective omission.
- The decision table reports p50 and p95 total time, critical-path change, queue delta, proof parity, cost per run, and cost per critical-path minute saved.
- No lane is adopted unless it meets the plan's improvement, parity, reliability, queue, canary, and owner-approved cost thresholds.
- Required-check names, branch protection, exact-head evidence, validation breadth, and result semantics are unchanged.
- Routing can return to `ubuntu-latest` without product-code or test-expectation changes, and rejected configuration is cleaned up.
- The final exact-head review has no unresolved actionable findings and the implementation PR includes `Closes #<this issue>`.

## Non-goals
- Do not use AWS or introduce a self-hosted runner platform.
- Do not make larger runners the organization-wide default.
- Do not change test logic, validation breadth, required-check names, or branch protection to manufacture a speedup.
- Do not test 32-core, coverage-topology, custom-image, ARM64, or self-hosted candidates unless separately authorized by a measured follow-up issue.
- Do not treat hardware, cache presence, runner provisioning, or planning prose as proof of acceleration.
